title: SDK TLS renegotiation + retry interplay causing customer 5xx waves (Host/Dedicated bridge)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Several enterprise customers reported sudden 502/504 waves during heavy request bursts that coincided with Dedicated gateway upgrades. Root cause investigation shows that TLS renegotiation events on Dedicated edge gateways triggered connection resets in the frontdoor proxy; our official SDKs then applied aggressive retry semantics causing amplifying request storms and backend queue saturation. This ticket coordinates a short-term mitigation, a targeted runtime patch, and a planned canary rollout with observability to prevent recurrences.

Timeline & evidence: 2025-02-16 03:40 UTC - customer A reported spike. Traces (Grafana panel 'hosted:5xx-by-tenant') show clustered 502s aligned with gateway upgrade window. Packet-level traces from gateway team show TLS renegotiation handshake failures at 03:37. SDK telemetry indicates retry loops restarting on connection reset with no idempotency guard (see sdk/telemetry/retries).

Root cause hypothesis: Dedicated gateway TLS session renegotiations (triggered by config reloads and client session TTL expiry) close underlying sockets. Frontdoor proxy interprets these as transient network errors. Our SDKs, by default, reissue full request payloads without per-request dedup tokens and with stacked backoff schedules, so a single connection churn event produced Nx retried requests in-flight to the same model-serving pool, producing head-of-line blocking and 5xx responses.

Immediate mitigations (short-term):
- Apply frontdoor tweak: lower concurrent retry concurrency window and enable per-connection healthy-probe delay (rolled at 2025-02-19 08:15). See PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/frontdoor/pull/614.
- Patch SDK: push opt-in client-level idempotency token and default retry leash to 2 for host-sensitive clients. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/211. Canary release scheduled for 2025-02-26.
- Customer comms: proactive notice sent to affected customers with temporary guidance to pin SDK version or set REDWOOD_MAX_RETRIES=1. Customer status thread: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/esc-1423.

Planned engineering work (this ticket):
1) Implement server-side detection of TLS-reneg-triggered resets and mark affected upstream connections stale for 30s to prevent immediate reconnect storms (runtime patch runtime-1.22).
2) Add per-tenant retry-leash and cross-service retry-header propagation (X-Redwood-Retry-Id) to permit dedup at the serving runtime.
3) Expand SDK defaults to include idempotency token generation for non-streaming requests and add opt-out flag.
4) End-to-end integration test that simulates TLS renegotiation with a controlled connection-close and validates no >1 retry per original logical request.

Rollout strategy: staged canary (10% traffic -> 30% -> 100%) across hosted and Dedicated gateway pools, gated on the following SLO checks (5xx rate, p95 latency, retry amplification ratio) for 30 minutes per stage. Canary automation plan: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollouts/blob/main/canary-playbooks/tls-retry.md.

Acceptance criteria:
- 5xx rate returns to baseline within 5 minutes for canary traffic during synthetic churn tests.
- No customer-visible retry amplification greater than 1.5x baseline.
- SDK opt-in telemetry demonstrates idempotency header present in >90% of canary requests.

Follow-ups & owners:
- Runtime patch: Marco Ruiz (owner).
- SDK changes: Priya Nair (owner) with review from Chen Li.
- Frontdoor probes and config: Sofia Andersson (owner).

Postmortem & learning: link to draft RCA: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/rca-2025/tls-retry-waves. We will run a retrospective with SRE, SDK, and Gateway teams to agree on default safe retry profiles and add a playbook to proactively throttle SDK behavior during gateway upgrade windows.
